text:
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from transient intent. [DSRec (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) closely matches this direction: historical aggregation feeds a long-term Mamba branch, while a separate short-term state-space branch adjusts state evolution using inter-click gaps; residual cross-fusion exchanges context. [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling (online 2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) instead maintains multiple long-term preference vectors through dynamic routing, selects those relevant to recent self-attention features, and combines them with time encoding. Useful principle: recent intent should select relevant persistent interests rather than uniformly pooling history.

Adaptive fusion also addresses unreliable interactions. [Stability-aware Preference Modeling (2025 manuscript)](https://cis.temple.edu/~jiewu/research/publications/Publication_files/2025-TWeb-Stability-aware%20Preference%20Modeling%20for%20Sequential%20Recommendation.pdf) extracts long/short interests with a multi-head GRU and fuses candidate information according to stability scores. [DiffLSRec (2026)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v318/wang26a.html) treats long-term preference as a prior and short-term intent as guidance during iterative denoising; conceptually relevant, but iterative diffusion adds computation.

Implementation inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec and add two inexpensive prefix-only states—a slowly updated preference memory and a fast, timestamp-decayed intent memory—with a learned scoring gate. Embedding disagreement and elapsed time could control fast-state resets while protecting persistent memory. Explicit change-point resetting was not established by the closest retrieved papers; treat it as an experimental extension. Train from scratch with next-item supervision using histories and timestamps. Enforce prefix-only computation at every supervised position: efficient SSM methods are not automatically causal—[SSD4Rec (2024/2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01192), for example, uses bidirectional blocks.
